title: In Situ Cryogenic 4D-STEM of 1T-TaS2 for Chiral Charge Density Wave Domain Characterization
content: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) as quantum materials have garnered much attention for hosting a variety of emergent phases including superconductivity, topological insulating phases, and charge density waves (CDWs) [1]. Progress in these systems is limited by a lack of understanding of the interplay between microstructure and emergent phases, which is critical for controlling these phases for eventual applications based on unconventional superconductivity, topological physics, and chiroptics. While real space probes such as scanning tunneling microscopy have been utilized, being a strictly surface-sensitive measurement places a fundamental limitation for scanning probes, requiring the utilization of more comprehensive techniques. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) can image the microstructure of the entire sample with high spatial resolution while in situ holders enable application of electric field and temperature control to manipulate emergent phases (Figure 1A) [2].
